skills.name: Z.AI (Zhipu GLM) Provider Config — OpenAI-Compatible Format
skills.description: Z.AI (bigmodel.cn / zhipuai.cn) uses OpenAI-compatible /chat/completions API. Setting api type to "anthropic-messages" appends /v1/messages and causes 404 errors. Always use openai-completions.
skills.body:
# Z.AI Provider Config — Use OpenAI-Compatible Format

## Problem

When configuring Z.AI (Zhipu AI / bigmodel.cn) as an LLM provider in OpenClaw (or any proxy that lets you choose API format), setting:

```json
"api": "anthropic-messages"
```

causes the request URL to be built as:

```
https://open.bigmodel.cn/api/paas/v4/v1/messages   ← 404
```

because `anthropic-messages` appends `/v1/messages` to the base URL.

Z.AI does **not** implement the Anthropic Messages API. It uses OpenAI-compatible endpoints.

---

## Fix

Set the api type to `openai-completions`:

```json
{
  "provider": "zai",
  "model": "glm-4-plus",
  "api": "openai-completions",
  "baseUrl": "https://open.bigmodel.cn/api/paas/v4",
  "apiKey": "YOUR_ZHIPU_API_KEY"
}
```

This routes requests to:
```
https://open.bigmodel.cn/api/paas/v4/chat/completions   ← correct
```

---

## Model names (Z.AI / Zhipu)

| Model | Notes |
|-------|-------|
| `glm-4-plus` | Most capable, primary model |
| `glm-4-flash` | Fast/cheap, good for high-volume tasks |
| `glm-4-long` | 128k context window |
| `glm-4v` | Vision (image understanding) |

---

## Fallback pattern

When z.ai balance runs out (rate limit error), fall back to OpenAI:

```json
{
  "provider": "openai",
  "model": "gpt-4o-mini",
  "api": "openai-completions"
}
```

Restore glm-4-plus as primary once z.ai account is topped up.

---

## Example Domains

| Platform | Applies? |
|----------|----------|
| OpenClaw / clawdbot LLM provider config | Yes — primary context |
| Any OpenAI-compatible proxy (LiteLLM, OpenRouter) | Yes — use openai format |
| Direct HTTP calls to bigmodel.cn | Yes — POST to /chat/completions |
| Vercel AI SDK | Yes — use `openai` provider with custom baseURL |

skills.name: Z.AI GLM Coding Plan + Claude Code (Anthropic-Compatible Endpoint, Per-Slot Model Mapping)
skills.description: Configure Claude Code to use Z.AI's GLM Coding Plan (Lite / Pro / Max subscription) via the Anthropic-compatible endpoint at api.z.ai/api/anthropic. Differs from Z.AI's OpenAI-format pay-as-you-go path - this is the subscription path with quota-based pricing instead of token-based, and uses three separate model slot env vars (ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_OPUS_MODEL / SONNET / HAIKU) instead of the singular ANTHROPIC_MODEL. API keys must be created AFTER the subscription is active or they will fail with error 1113 even when quota is available.
skills.body:
# Z.AI GLM Coding Plan + Claude Code

## When to use

You have an active Z.AI **GLM Coding Plan** subscription (Lite $18/mo, Pro $72/mo, or
Max ~$160/mo - tiers may shift) and want Claude Code to draw from that quota instead
of pay-as-you-go API credits.

This is **not** the same as using Z.AI's OpenAI-compatible endpoint. The Coding Plan
gates a separate Anthropic-compatible endpoint specifically for Claude Code, Goose,
Cline, OpenCode, and a few other officially supported tools.

See also: `zai-openai-compatible-provider` (OpenAI-format, for pay-as-you-go usage
outside the Coding Plan).

## Critical setup order

1. **Subscribe first.** Active GLM Coding Plan must exist on the account.
2. **Create the API key AFTER subscription is active.** Existing keys do not auto-bind
   to a new subscription. If a key was minted before the plan was attached (or in a
   pay-as-you-go context), API calls return error `1113 "Insufficient balance"` even
   though the dashboard shows the plan as Valid with full quota. Regenerate to fix.
3. Configure Claude Code (env vars OR `~/.claude/settings.json`).

## Endpoint and headers

| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| Base URL | `https://api.z.ai/api/anthropic` |
| Auth env var | `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN` (Claude Code converts to `Authorization: Bearer <token>`) |
| Auth header sent | `Authorization: Bearer <token>` |
| API version header | not required for the Coding Plan endpoint |

## Model slot mapping (per Z.AI's official docs)

Claude Code routes different request types to "Opus" / "Sonnet" / "Haiku" slots
internally. Z.AI maps each slot to a GLM model via three env vars:

```bash
export ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL="https://api.z.ai/api/anthropic"
export ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN="<your-zai-coding-plan-key>"
export ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_OPUS_MODEL="GLM-4.7"      # complex reasoning slot
export ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_SONNET_MODEL="GLM-4.7"    # default coding slot
export ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_HAIKU_MODEL="GLM-4.5-Air" # sub-agent / fast slot
```

**Do NOT use** the singular `ANTHROPIC_MODEL` / `ANTHROPIC_SMALL_FAST_MODEL` here -
the Coding Plan endpoint expects per-slot routing. Singular vars work for DeepSeek
and pay-as-you-go but not for the GLM Coding Plan path.

## Available models on the Coding Plan

| Model | Slot fit | Quota cost |
|-------|----------|------------|
| `GLM-4.7` | Sonnet/Opus default - daily coding | 1x quota |
| `GLM-4.5-Air` | Haiku default - fast sub-agent | 1x quota |
| `GLM-4.5` | Older sonnet-tier | 1x quota |
| `GLM-5.1` | Premium opus-equivalent | 3x peak / 2x off-peak (1x off-peak through Jun 2026 promo) |
| `GLM-5-Turbo` | Premium opus-equivalent | same as GLM-5.1 |

Peak hours: 14:00-18:00 UTC+8.

## Plan quotas (recheck against current docs - tiers shift)

| Plan | 5-hour cap | Weekly cap |
|------|------------|------------|
| Lite | ~80 prompts | ~400 prompts |
| Pro | ~400 prompts | ~2,000 prompts |
| Max | ~1,600 prompts | ~8,000 prompts |

One "prompt" = one user query, internally fanning out to 15-20 model calls.

## Diagnosing error 1113 "Insufficient Balance"

Per Z.AI's official FAQ, error 1113 has three possible causes when subscription is
valid:

1. **Tool not on the supported list.** SDK-style direct calls (curl, raw Anthropic
   SDK without the right user-agent) may be rejected. Use Claude Code, Cline,
   Goose, OpenCode, OpenClaw, etc.
2. **Wrong base URL.** Coding Plan only accepts `https://api.z.ai/api/anthropic` for
   Claude Code/Goose, or `https://api.z.ai/api/coding/paas/v4` for other tools.
3. **API key not bound to the plan.** Most common. Key was created before the plan
   was attached. Regenerate at `https://z.ai/manage-apikey/apikey-list`.

If the dashboard at `https://z.ai/manage-apikey/subscription` shows 0% / 0% / 0%
across all quotas after sustained attempts, it's almost certainly cause #3.

## Recommended `~/.claude/settings.json` (per-user config alternative)

```json
{
  "env": {
    "ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL": "https://api.z.ai/api/anthropic",
    "ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN": "your_zai_api_key",
    "API_TIMEOUT_MS": "3000000",
    "CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_NONESSENTIAL_TRAFFIC": 1,
    "ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_OPUS_MODEL": "glm-5.1",
    "ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_SONNET_MODEL": "glm-4.7",
    "ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_HAIKU_MODEL": "glm-4.5-air"
  }
}
```

Choose env vars (per-shell, toggleable) OR settings.json (per-user, always-on). Don't
mix - settings.json wins and overrides env vars in some Claude Code versions.

## Verification

```bash
# Direct curl test (works for Claude Code-launched key, may be restricted for raw SDK):
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $ZAI_KEY" \
     -H "content-type: application/json" \
     -d '{"model":"GLM-4.7","max_tokens":40,"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hi"}]}' \
     "https://api.z.ai/api/anthropic/v1/messages"

# Expected: HTTP 200 with {"id":"msg_...","model":"glm-4.7","content":[...]}
# Failure: HTTP 429 with {"error":{"code":"1113",...}}
```

## Switching back

```bash
unset ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN \
      ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_OPUS_MODEL \
      ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_SONNET_MODEL \
      ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_HAIKU_MODEL
```

## Example Domains

| Domain | Applies? |
|--------|----------|
| Claude Code with GLM Coding Plan subscription | Yes - primary case |
| Goose / Cline / OpenCode / OpenClaw with same Coding Plan key | Yes - same endpoint |
| Z.AI pay-as-you-go API (no subscription) | No - use OpenAI-format endpoint instead, see related skill |
| Migrating from old `glm-4.6` config to Coding Plan models | Yes - replace singular ANTHROPIC_MODEL with the three slot vars |

## Anti-patterns

- Using singular `ANTHROPIC_MODEL=glm-4.6` - GLM-4.6 doesn't exist; use GLM-4.7 in the three-slot mapping.
- Reusing a pre-subscription API key - regenerate after subscribing.
- Mixing settings.json + env vars - settings.json silently wins in some versions.
- Direct curl probes with arbitrary user-agents - Coding Plan may flag as unsupported and 1113 even when key is valid.

skills.name: Zero-Hardcode Bottom-Up Integration Protocol
skills.description: 5-step mandatory build order for any data-display feature — Backend → Verify → Store → UI → Traceability. Prevents AI from hallucinating a "finished" UI with hardcoded demo data by forcing verification of the real data path before any frontend work begins.
skills.body: # Zero-Hardcode Bottom-Up Integration Protocol ## Problem When asked to build a feature (dashboard widget, data table, live chart, HMI panel), AI coding assistants default to the **"Agentic Shortcut"**: they build the complete UI immediately with hardcoded demo data because it's faster and looks finished. The result: - `useState([{ id: 1, name: "Demo Pump", value: 72.4 }])` — fake data that never gets replaced - Connected status shown even when API is down - Beautiful UI that breaks immediately in production - Hours of debugging to find where real data was supposed to come from ## Solution — The 5-Step Bottom-Up Protocol Force this exact order. **Never skip. Never reorder.** --- ## The 5 Steps ### Step 1 — Backend + Schema First Build only the data layer. Nothing else. ``` - Create the database model / Prisma schema - Create the service/repository function - Create the API endpoint (if needed) - For real-time: create the polling/subscription service DO NOT: touch React, Zustand, Redux, or any UI file OUTPUT: schema + service code only ``` ### Step 2 — Verify the Data Path (mandatory gate) Run a test or curl that proves real data flows. **You must see real data before proceeding.** ```bash # Option A — direct service test npx vitest run src/services/tags.test.ts # Option B — curl the endpoint curl http://localhost:3000/api/tags/1 # Option C — Python script python3 -c "from services.contacts import get_all; print(get_all())" ``` **Gate rule:** If the output shows real data → proceed to Step 3. If it fails → fix the backend. Do NOT move forward with a broken pipe. ### Step 3 — Frontend Store (Zustand / Redux / Context) Wire the store to the verified endpoint. **Required fields:** ```typescript interface TagStore { data: Tag | null; // real data or null — never fake default loading: boolean; // true while fetching error: string | null; // error message or null fetch: (id: string) => Promise; } const useTagStore = create((set) => ({ data: null, // NOT: { id: 1, value: 72.4 } loading: false, error: null, fetch: async (id) => { set({ loading: true, error: null }); try { const data = await api.get(`/tags/${id}`); set({ data, loading: false }); } catch (e) { set({ error: e.message, loading: false, data: null }); } }, })); ``` ### Step 4 — UI Components Build the display layer. **Hardcoding is forbidden.** ```tsx // ✅ CORRECT — real states function TagDisplay({ id }: { id: string }) { const { data, loading, error } = useTagStore(); if (loading) return ; if (error) return ; if (!data) return No Data; // NOT a hardcoded value return {data.value} {data.unit}; } // ❌ FORBIDDEN — fake data function TagDisplay() { const [value] = useState(72.4); // hardcoded return {value} bar; // looks fine, never wired } ``` **Required states every data component must handle:** - `loading` — show spinner or skeleton - `error` — show error message, not fake data - `empty/null` — show "No Data" or "Disconnected" - `live` — show real value ### Step 5 — Traceability Comments Every component that displays data gets one traceability line: ```tsx // DATA SOURCE: GET /api/tags/:id → tag_readings.value → useTagStore().data.value function PressureGauge({ tagId }) { ... } // DATA SOURCE: Supabase bni_contacts.status → useContactStore().contacts[].status function ContactStatusBadge({ contactId }) { ... } ``` --- ## The Protocol as a Prompt Paste this when starting any data-display feature: ``` I want to implement [Feature Name]. Follow the Zero-Hardcode Protocol: Step 1: Backend + Schema only. No UI yet. Step 2: Write a verification command (test/curl/script) I can run to see real data. WAIT for me to confirm real data before proceeding. Step 3: Zustand/store with data/loading/error states. No hardcoded defaults. Step 4: UI components. No hardcoding. Missing data = "No Data" state. Step 5: Add // DATA SOURCE comments to every data-bound component. Start with Step 1 only. ``` --- ## Why It Works | Without Protocol | With Protocol | |-----------------|---------------| | Broken pipeline found after 10 components built | Broken pipeline found in Step 2 (before any UI) | | Hardcoded data that "works in demo" | Real data or honest empty state | | No idea where data comes from | Every component has a DATA SOURCE comment | | 3 hours of debugging | 20 minutes of fixing at the right layer | --- ## Example Domains | Feature | Step 1 artifact | Step 2 verification | |---------|----------------|---------------------| | SCADA live tag display | Prisma TagReading model + polling service | `curl /api/tags/PLC1_PRESSURE` → real value | | BNI contact status table | Supabase query function | `python3 -c "print(get_contacts())"` | | WhatsApp message history | DB query + REST endpoint | `curl /api/messages?phone=+91...` | | Dashboard metric card | Aggregation query + service | `npx vitest run metrics.test.ts` | | Real-time chart | WebSocket tag subscription | Console log showing live values |
